Vacate 40 first (S01-F02; target number per D-S01-13), git mv 42->40, 43->42, 44->43, 45->44, 46->45, 47->46, rewrite the full old folder names in the 67 files of parity/verify_s01/renumber_touch_verified.txt in one pass (each name is unique, so the pass is collision-safe), bump the WCP SW token, add a ledger 'Folder renumbering' section and dated revision notes to VV D05 (and to TV plan 4/4.1 if D-S01-12 allows TV edits).

title: CrossSection__SceneData positionMm sign is opposite in the two apps (TD06 not met)
detail: VV writes positionMm = -plane.constant and restores the plane through normal*positionMm (constant = -positionMm). TV writes +plane.constant and restores constant = +positionMm. The same {normalXyz, positionMm} therefore builds planes mirrored through the world origin: a TV plan cut at 1200 would restore in VV at y = -1200. Each app round-trips its own data. Code reading only, not executed.
recommendation: No VV change. Fix TV to VV's convention (TD06 says VV's schema wins, and TV's own mapping table says -constant), and migrate TV's saved bindings. Add a cross-app fixture test once fixed. Adam decides.
evidence:
- VVM/41/Na__CrossSectionView__SystemLogic.js: :1502 (serialize -constant), :1540-1542 (restore point = normal*positionMm), :567 (plane through point).
- VVM/42/Na__DrawView__SectionAdapter__.js:298-300: the plan cut has normal (0,-1,0) and position -cutHeight, so constant = +cutHeight and positionMm = -cutHeight.
- TVM/41/Na__SectionCut__Serialize__.js:194 writes +constant. The comment above it claims 'the two engines store plane.constant with opposite signs for the same normal'. That is false: a THREE.Plane's constant is fixed by its normal and position, and both engines build plan cuts with normal (0,-1,0) and constant +h. TV's round-trip test only proves TV to TV.
- TV realign plan: the example at line 217 (positionMm 1200) contradicts the mapping row at line 245 (-record.plane.constant).
verifier_note: Confirmed by re-derivation, but there is no live fault (neither app reads the other's projects) and no VV change is proposed. It matters only for cross-app documents or a careless verbatim port of TV's Serialize. | Adds the VV SectionAdapter path and the TV-side evidence of why the sign diverged, which strengthens the decision for Adam.

title: Thumbnail capture signature differs: ported TV editors cannot take the Update picture, and VV's batch thumbnails already fail
detail:
The two apps' Na__PresentationMode__Thumbnail__CaptureAndUpload take different arguments:
- TV: (sceneId, targetWidthPx), writing through Na__CfApi__WriteThumbnailWebp.
- VV: (sceneId, projectCode, showToast), which returns { ok:false, error:'missing scene id or project code' } when no project code is passed.
TV's 2.x editors call it with the scene id only. Ported whole (WP-08), every Update would toast 'Thumbnail upload failed' and leave the card's picture unchanged. The survey's name-only import check cannot see this; sigcheck.py (parameter counts) found it.
The same fault is already live in VV: VV's ported Presentation Scenes batch op calls it with one argument, and that op is wired to Update All Thumbnails. By code reading, every batch thumbnail fails in VV today. Not run.
recommendation: Make VV's CaptureAndUpload accept TV's call shape. When the second argument is not a string, resolve the project code itself (Na__PresentationMode__ProjectJson__GetActiveProjectCode, falling back to Na__AppUtils__GetProjectCodeFromUrl), and treat a numeric second argument as targetWidthPx. Keep (sceneId, projectCode, showToast) working for ScenePersistence, ThumbnailBake and the 1.x editors. This fixes VV's Update All Thumbnails now, and lets TV's editors (and TV's scene editor) port verbatim. Land it before WP-08. Ask Adam to confirm the batch failure with one press on localhost, before and after.
evidence: TVM/21/Na__PresentationMode__Thumbnail__Renderer.js:261; VVM/21/Na__PresentationMode__Thumbnail__Renderer.js:229-231; TVM/42/Na__FloorPlan__DevMenu__Editor__.js:858; TVM/45/Na__Elevation__DevMenu__Editor__.js:992; VVM/21/Na__PresentationMode__DevMenu__BatchOps__.js:353 wired at VVM/21/Na__PresentationMode__DevMenu__SceneEditor.js:1360; parity/verify_s02a/sigcheck.py output.
vv_adaptation: Transport stays VV's: Na__AppUtils__R2AssetUpload to PresentationMode/Thumbnails/<scene id>.webp, R2 first then the Flask mirror.

title: Shared service-worker token must be bumped for the renumber and every export-changing S02a WP
detail:
In production, VV's shell JS and CSS are served stale-while-revalidate by the shared WebApps worker, keyed on PWA_SW_VERSION_TOKEN ('2026-09-18-1', WCP/02__Src__AppModules/62__Feature__AppInstallability/Whitecardopedia__Pwa__ServiceWorker__Logic__.js:229). The VV ledger (lines 161-175) records four VV releases that added cross-module exports without a bump.
Every S02a WP adds or moves exports, and WP-01 moves about 70 module paths. Until its next load, a warm client can run an old cached index.html or LE module that imports a path or name that no longer exists.
TV bumped its own worker token for v2.86.0 for exactly this reason (devlog: 'Service worker token 2026-09-20-3: new exports on files a warm cache already holds').
recommendation: Each S02a WP records 'token needed' in its devlog entry. Bump the token once per VV release wave that ships them. It is Adam's call, because the token evicts every Vale app's caches (D-S09-06). The renumber release must not ship without the bump.
evidence: WCP/.../Whitecardopedia__Pwa__ServiceWorker__Logic__.js:229; VV/ValeVision__PARITY__TrueVisionLedger__.md:161-175; TV devlog v2.86.0 Files list (line ~7914); S09 D-S09-06.

title: Depth fog and projected vectors: on screen neither app fogs the SVG overlay; VV exports put vectors above the fog
detail:

recommendation: Correct the WP-S02b-04 acceptance (done in WP-S02b-04R). Ask Adam (D-S02b-V02) whether VV image exports should match sheets. title: Barrel ahead of its units breaks module linking
detail: TV's ConfigState barrel (1.29.0) statically imports four names from ConfigState__KeyMap__ (TV ConfigState__.js:236-253): ReloadKeyMap, GetCopyDragModifier, GetMoveAnchorModifier and IsCopyDragKey. It also imports GetVectorQualitySetup, GetPlanDoorsSetup, GetModelSourceSetup, GetDrawingRegisterSetup and GetStatementSetup from SheetSetup/EditorSetup. An ES module fails at link time when a named import is missing. WP-S03a-01 takes 'the six ConfigState files' while WP-S03a-02 ports KeyMap later. Taking TV's barrel while VV's KeyMap is still 1.0.0 would stop the whole editor loading, behind the VV loader's error screen. The barrel's code differs from VV's only in these nine names (git diff -w).

The four KeyMap names go with KeyMap 1.11.0 and the key-file rename (WP-S03a-02). Gate every config package on Na__Verify__Exports__.mjs (it checks imported names) and Na__Verify__ModuleGraph__.mjs.

title: Selecting a viewport should fold the markup group (TV MC 1.21.0)
detail: TV's SectionForKind returns FOLD_GROUP ('') for a viewport, and FocusPanelFor(kind, items) then folds the whole accordion group ('if (section === null) return false; return FocusSection(section || null)'). So Text, Dimensions, Shapes and Leaders (and later Images, Floor Areas and Patterns) do not stand open over a selected drawing (TV ModeController__.js:1036,1048,1101,1107). VV's SectionForKind(kind) returns null for a viewport and leaves the folds as they were (VV ModeController__.js:736,754,759). VV's PanelHost FocusSection(null) already folds the whole group (VV PanelHost__.js:474), so the viewport rule does not depend on any TV-only feature. Only the single-site-plan -> 'patterns' branch and the areas/images branches wait for their features.
recommendation: In WP-S03a-V04, add the FOLD_GROUP constant, the two-argument SectionForKind/FocusPanelFor, and FocusPanelForSelection passing the expanded items, with the viewport rule. Leave the OneSitePlan, AllAreas and AllImages branches to the site plan, Floor Areas and Sheet Images packages.
evidence: TV ModeController__.js:1036 (FOLD_GROUP), :1048-1100 (SectionForKind, OneSitePlan, AllImages, AllAreas), :1101-1115; VV ModeController__.js:736-766; VV PanelHost__.js:474-485; TV ModeController 1.21.0 log

title: Transitions opt-in would strip the Walk exit from VV's plan and elevation entries
detail: VV Transitions 1.0.0 SuspendThreeD() always leaves Walk/Fly, through Na__NavToolbar__SetOrbitMode. Three VV callers rely on that: the Layout Editor (ModeController:524), the floor plan controller (43/Na__FloorPlan__ModeController__.js:465) and the elevation controller (46/Na__Elevation__ModeController__.js:526). A fourth caller, the snapshot renderer (51/25/Na__LayoutEditor__SnapshotRenderer__.js:501), does NOT want it. It suspends around every viewport picture, so a picture rendered from the 3D tab (a bake, a quiet re-stamp after a drawing rename) drops a walker back to Orbit. TV removed that behaviour in Transitions 1.1.0 (v2.112.0). TV's own plan and elevation controllers never call Transitions, so TV only had to pass the option from the Layout Editor (:707). S02a's WP-S02a-11 ports the opt-in and names only the Layout Editor caller.
recommendation: When Transitions 1.1.0 lands (S02a WP-S02a-11; ReturnToOrbit = VV's Na__NavToolbar__SetOrbitMode), pass { returnToOrbit : true } from all three VV drawing entries (Layout Editor, floor plan, elevation) in the same change. Leave the snapshot renderer call bare. Acceptance: entering a plan, an elevation or a drawing tab while walking leaves Walk; baking or re-stamping a viewport picture from the 3D tab while walking does not.
evidence: VV grep of Na__DrawView__Transitions__SuspendThreeD callers: 51 ModeController:524, 43 FloorPlan MC:465, 46 Elevation MC:526, 51/25 SnapshotRenderer:501. TV callers: LE ModeController:707 (with the option), SnapshotRenderer:905 (bare). TV Transitions 1.1.0 log; S02a WP-S02a-11.

title: VV 3D hotkey dictionary dispatches its documentation rows
detail: Na__ValeVision__HotkeysDictionary__.json holds ten ValeVision__DrawingMarkup__Contextual rows (D, O, Arrows, Alt, Shift, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V, Delete, Escape). They sit in the same array the handler dispatches, so that they can be listed in the help panel's Advanced fold. index.html registers no callback for that action, and the handler calls preventDefault BEFORE it dispatches (HotkeyHandler__.js:91-101). So a bare D, O, Delete or Escape, outside a text field and on any tab, is taken from the browser and logs 'No callback for action ValeVision__DrawingMarkup__Contextual' on every press. TV's 3D file keeps only dispatchable bindings in its array (15) and documents the context keys in separate reference blocks (Na__Hotkeys__Movement__Reference, Na__Hotkeys__Ui__Reference). Low impact today: the only VV listeners that check defaultPrevented are the mode controller's Ctrl+S handler and the Measurements box, and both run in the capture phase, before this handler.
recommendation: With the key-scope guard (WP-S03a-V03), skip any binding whose action has no registered callback before calling preventDefault. Alternatively, move the documentation rows into a reference block (TV's shape) and have the navigation help panel read it. Either way, keep the rows visible in VV's help panel.
evidence: VV 02__AppData/Na__ValeVision__HotkeysDictionary__.json (28 rows, 10 Contextual); VV HotkeyHandler__.js:74-82,91-101; VV index.html:1792-1809 (no Contextual callback); VV NavigationHelpPanel__Controls.js:292-294; TV 02__AppData/Na__Hotkeys__3dModelTab__.json (15 bindings plus reference blocks); grep: defaultPrevented checked only at ModeController:629 and Measurements:584

title: First drawing tab after a document-tab entry: TV veils it, VV does not
detail: TV's first-open veil runs once per session (Na__LeVeil__FirstUsed, LoadingVeil:124,317). It is skipped only for the quiet entry under a document tab (EnterUnder; Enter calls FirstOpen when !Quiet, ModeController:733). So when a session starts on the Specification, Register or Statements and the reader then opens a drawing, 'Your Drawings Are Loading' covers that first drawing while its viewports render. In VV the loader screen covers only the editor's first load; after that, WithEditor runs every action with no screen (Loader.js:388-422). A first drawing tab opened after a document tab therefore gets no cover. This becomes reachable once TabStrip 2.0.0 shows the document tabs from the 3D view.
recommendation: Decide with D-S03a-09 / D-S03a-11. For the same behaviour as TV, have the loader show its screen on the first sheet view of a session whose editor was first loaded for a document view, waiting on WaitForFirstDrawing. This is a loader-only change, with no second overlay.
evidence: TV ModeController__.js:722-737,883-888; TV LoadingVeil__.js:103,124,317; VV Loader__.js:376-422

Until a register exists, RenumberSheets is a no-op in VV; check R2 for typed numbers first. Then SheetRecords, Sheets, History, title block Rows and PdfExporter (code: fields.DocumentId) can be identical.

Back-porting it to TV is D-S03b-02, not a given: the leaf's own PORT NOTE says 'offer to TrueVision3D only if its tab strip is ever made lazy; until then the split would buy it nothing', so the case for it rests only on the identical-SheetRecords goal and needs Adam's yes. title: Likely VV bug: Common fields seed never runs on the first editor load
detail: VV lazy-loads the editor, so the model initialises after the drawings load. The loader then dispatches a synthetic 'loaded' on the model's own event (Loader L307-311, called at L339), bypassing reload(), the only caller of Na__LeModel__SeedCommonFields (SheetModel L504). Code-traced, not run: on first open the pack's client and site address are neither seeded nor migrated from the sheets, and because Na__LeCommon__Record is filled only by that seed (SheetModel__Common L266-282), the Sheet panel's project-record offer (RecordOffer) is empty too. VV also hears any later load twice (the facade listens to LOADED and CHANGED, L506-507, and ProjectData dispatches CHANGED from inside its LOADED handler, L208-216/L446-455), clearing the dirty flag a draft restore just set (TV v2.145 finding). VV's ModeController initialises model, History, AutoSave, Spec and SpecLinks in one synchronous pass (ModeController L831-835), so TV's microtask announce works unchanged in VV.
recommendation: Fixed by porting TV's facade Initialize and removing the loader's announcement (WP-S03b-04). Acceptance: on first open, a pack whose sheets share a client seeds CommonClient once, and 'loaded' is heard exactly once.
evidence: VV SheetModel L497-507; VV Loader L299-311, L339; VV ProjectData L446-455, L208-216 (CHANGED inside the LOADED handler); grep: SeedCommonFields only called at SheetModel L504; TV DEVLOG v2.145.0 L2006-2050.
verifier_note: Verifier traced a second symptom (empty record offer) and confirmed TV's late-start mechanism fits VV's init order.

title: Fog images need a callback route that VV's tiled renderer lacks (DIV-1)
detail: TV renders a drawing's fog image with Render2d(..., fogSource) -> RenderToCanvas({ renderFrame: Na__ElevFog__RenderLayerFrame }). VV's TiledRenderer 1.4.0 has no renderFrame option; TV's (now 2.1.0 - the callback route arrived in 2.0.0) has it at :232-:269. TV TiledRenderer's own PORT NOTE says 'the supersampling is worth carrying back; the callback route is not' - written before the fog image existed, so option (a) knowingly reverses it. TV devlog v2.94.0: 'Not in ValeVision ... the two draw calls land elsewhere there'. Separately, TV's 49 RenderLayer imports Na__SectionCut__RenderDepthInto from TV's section engine (:105, used :476), which neither VV's Cross Sections tool nor either SectionAdapter offers (S04a-V03), so the fog image also needs a VV DIV-2 route.
recommendation: D-S04a-05: add TV's optional renderFrame callback route to VV's tiled renderer, used only when a caller passes it (the fog image); the underlay keeps the composer route. Then port SnapshotRenderer's fog hunks, the Frame fog layer, RenderFogForExport, the Paper CSS .na-le-frame__fog rule and the PdfExporter fog.
evidence: VV TiledRenderer: no 'renderFrame'; TV TiledRenderer :232,:259,:269,:402,:421; TV devlog :7095-:7096.
verifier_note: TV TiledRenderer log shows 2.1.0; its PORT NOTE contradicts option (a); the RenderDepthInto dependency was missed.

title: ModelSource (TV-only, 305 lines, 1.1.0)

The payoff of a dormant port (whole-file takes of the viewport units) only fully arrives together with D-S04a-01 = B. TV's header has no PORT NOTE.

title: Site plans are the largest single source of shared-file drift
detail: TV's site plan system (v2.48.0-v2.164.0, plus 55014c6a) covers: a drawing type; two stores; a GLB parser; a three-deck painter; block and location plans; hatches; scales from 1:100 to 1:5000; style defaults; fill and dash overrides; scrapbook furniture; a legend; PDF, publishing and viewer support. About 27-30 TV files reference site plan APIs, depending on what is counted (30 with config, CSS and the service worker). Since TV v2.158.0 (TabStrip 2.0.0) site plans are marked rows of the Drawings menu, not a tab group after the plus. VV has none of it. TV's composites plan 3.5 says any VV port is 'a surgical merge of the non-site-plan parts only', because a whole-file copy of the painter, EdgeStyles, SheetRecords or ScaleManager imports Na__SpStore__*; option B overrides that standing guidance deliberately and the decision text should say so. TV ledger P10, 'offer the ValeVision port', has not been started.
recommendation: D-S04a-01 option B: port the client side dormant - modules verbatim, a VV transport adapter, VV stems, and a VV config flag that hides the Drawing Type row until a Vale pipeline exists. Decide the Vale data pipeline separately (F41).
evidence: grep of site plan APIs in TV M/: 27 files; TV PLAN__SitePlanComposites 3.5 and ledger P10; VV ledger :78,:79,:1166,:1181,:1184 ('one drawing type').
verifier_note: TabStrip 2.0.0 (v2.158.0) changed the tab grouping; TV's own plan 3.5 guidance was not cited.

Test Na__Test__SitePlanStore__ (32).

title: VV SheetRecords loses three of this slice's fields and ignores the rest
detail: VV's normalisers mutate records in place and keep unknown top-level keys, so a TV record keeps Viewport__RotationDeg, Viewport__ClosedDoors, Viewport__HideSwings, Viewport__ModelSourceId, the Viewport__SitePlan block, Sheet__DrawingType and Asset__Samples (inside the kept snapshot slot) through a VV save - VV simply ignores them. What VV does lose: Viewport__Styles is rebuilt from its eight known keys (depthFog dropped; VV :415-:424, STYLE_KEYS :214), and NormaliseProjectedEdges rebuilds each category entry from Label/Weight/Colour/LineType (Category__LineTypeScale and Category__FillHex dropped) and clamps weight factors to VV's Weight__Max 3.00 (TV 10.00). The composite-weight normaliser is identical in both apps and driven by RenderComposites rows, so the percent Enhance weight needs no SheetRecords change. TV SheetRecords 1.39.0 vs VV 1.15.0.
recommendation: Each feature WP adds its keys to SheetRecords and SheetModel (owned by the SheetData slice; serialise these edits). Keep TV's rule of storing a key only while it is non-default, so old records stay byte-identical.
evidence: grep counts in LE/07 SheetRecords (TV 1.39.0 vs VV 1.15.0); TV :427,:1019,:1038-:1062; VV :214.
verifier_note: VV's normalisers keep unknown top-level keys. | VV NormaliseViewport, NormaliseSheet, NormaliseProjectedEdges and NormaliseCompositeWeights read in full. | Only three fields are lost, and the two apps do not share project files in practice.

title: TONE import trap: repointing a VV caller without dropping TONE breaks module linking
detail: VV PointerDrag (:137) and DimensionTool (:129) import Na__LeOsnap__TONE_DIMENSION. TV Search exports no TONE names, and an ES module import of a missing named export is a link-time SyntaxError that blanks the whole lazily-loaded editor. TV Search.Snap and Marker.ShowMarker silently ignore a legacy tone argument, so the call sites themselves need no change.
recommendation: Either drop the TONE import in the same edit as the repoint, or keep the Snapping__ shim exporting TONE_VERTEX/DIMENSION/VIEWPORT as local string constants for one wave (D-S04b-09, WP-S04b-06R). The shim imports only __Search__ and __State__, never the controller. Gate every step with Na__Verify__Exports__.mjs.
evidence: VV PointerDrag:137, DimensionTool:129, :172, :243, :291, :316, PointerDrag:343; TV Search exports :627-654; Search:506-514 (legacy arg).
verifier_note: Aligns the trap's fix with the cycle-free shim (S04b-V02).

title: VV runs under the shared Whitecardopedia service worker: each wave needs Adam's token decision
detail: Refutes F49. VV index.html:44 loads ../Whitecardopedia/02__Src__AppModules/62__Feature__AppInstallability/Whitecardopedia__Pwa__ServiceWorker__Registrar__.js. It registers the WebApps-root stub Na__Pwa__ServiceWorker__.js, which importScripts Whitecardopedia__Pwa__ServiceWorker__Logic__.js ('Caching brain of the Whitecardopedia + ValeVision3D PWA'). On VV's live https origin (adam-noble-01.github.io), shell JS/CSS is served stale-while-revalidate against PWA_SW_VERSION_TOKEN = '2026-09-18-1' (:229); on localhost it is network-first. The worker's own log records token bumps for VV Layout Editor releases (1.0.5 to 1.0.8) and a mixed old/new module graph failing to link ('does not provide an export named ...', 1.0.7). VV's ledger corrected its own 'n/a - this tree has no PWA worker' rows (:135-175), and VV devlog v2.67-v2.71 end with 'THE SHARED SERVICE WORKER' notes. This slice adds 31 modules, puts new exports on Measurements, SheetSurface, SheetModel, SheetModel__Layers and ShapeGeometry in the seam wave alone, and repoints 10 importers: exactly that failure. Bumping the token evicts every Vale app's caches, models included, so it is Adam's call, and the file is outside VV's tree. The worker's best-effort precache lists only VV start-up modules, none in 51__System__LayoutEditor, so deleting Snapping__.js cannot break its install.
recommendation: No WP edits the Whitecardopedia worker. Every WP of this slice ends its VV devlog entry with a 'THE SHARED SERVICE WORKER' note naming the new modules and the new exports on existing modules. Ledger return-trip rows record 'Service worker token: shared Whitecardopedia worker - Adam's call', never 'n/a'. Raise one bump request with Adam per deployed wave (D-S04b-V01, WP-S04b-16).
evidence: VV index.html:19 (manifest), :44 (registrar); D:\10_CoreLib__ValeCodebase\WebApps\Whitecardopedia\02__Src__AppModules\62__Feature__AppInstallability\Whitecardopedia__Pwa__ServiceWorker__Logic__.js:9, :22, :85-108 (1.0.7, 1.0.8 log), :229 (token), :260 (precache list: VV start-up modules only); D:\10_CoreLib__ValeCodebase\WebApps\Na__Pwa__ServiceWorker__.js:14-31; VV ledger :89-93, :135-175; VV devlog :91, :194, :473-478; TV devlog v2.111 'Service worker' (5477-5479) shows the same reasoning in TV.

title: A Snapping__ shim must not re-export the controller (module cycle through Measurements)
detail: The survey's shim (F02, WP-S04b-06, D-S04b-09) re-exports 'the new names from Search, Marker and the controller'. The controller imports Measurements for Say (ObjectSnap__.js:99), and VV Measurements__.js:118-120 imports ShapeTool, RectangleTool and DimensionTool, all of which import Snapping__.js. Routing Toggle/SetEnabled through the shim creates tools -> Snapping -> controller -> Measurements -> tools, the cycle TV's ObjectSnap__.js:33-37 exists to avoid ('a tool importing it would close a cycle'). VV Measurements calls the tools only inside function bodies, so it would probably not throw today, but it is a latent TDZ trap, and Na__Verify__ModuleGraph__.mjs checks resolution only, not cycles. Only Keyboard:123, Toolbar:110 and ContextMenu:100 import Toggle; no VV module imports SetEnabled, KIND_END or KIND_MID. TV State exports CHANGED_EVENT and IsEnabled; Search re-exports IsEnabled, Find, Snap, Clear, ShowMarker and HideMarker. Compatibility of the unchanged VV call sites was verified: Search.Snap ignores a string 4th argument (:506-512), ShowMarker(hit) ignores a 2nd, Marker.TargetOf (:141-146) colours tone-less hits (infer -> dimension, else -> shape), and TV's exclusion shapes are VV's (Sources:414-457).
recommendation: The shim imports only from __Search__ (Find, Snap, ShowMarker, HideMarker, Clear, IsEnabled, KIND_END, KIND_MID) and __State__ (CHANGED_EVENT), with TONE_VERTEX/DIMENSION/VIEWPORT as local strings. In the same commit, repoint Keyboard:123, Toolbar:110 and ContextMenu:100 to ../28__System__ObjectSnap/Na__LayoutEditor__ObjectSnap__.js and ModeController:228 to __Search__ (WP-S04b-06R). Acceptance: grep shows no import of Na__LayoutEditor__ObjectSnap__.js from the shim or from 35__System__DrawingTools.
evidence: TV ObjectSnap__.js:33-37, :99; VV Measurements__.js:118-120 (tool calls only inside functions: :405-665); VV Toggle importers Keyboard:123, Toolbar:110, ContextMenu:100, Clear importer ModeController:228; TV State and Search export lists; VV Na__Verify__ModuleGraph__.mjs:13-20 (resolution walk only).

title: Viewport carry needs TV-only CarryTarget in HitResolution and mandatory config keys
detail: Na__LeTools__CarryTarget ('the viewport a press may carry by a point', null when a handle, the rotate grip, content editing, a lock or a multi-selection owns the press) is TV-only code in TV SheetTools__HitResolution__.js:753-768, exported :797. The TV port note (:49) lists it as a TrueVision divergence. PointerPress:353 calls it before GrabAt, and PointerDrag's hover calls it too. VV recorded leaving it out (SheetTools__.js:257-258, 'this tree has no viewport carry yet'), and WP-S04b-11 does not list HitResolution. It reads Editable, GetSelectionItems, IsSelected, GetEditingViewport, GetViewportById and IsViewportLocked: VV HitResolution has all but GetSelectionItems and IsSelected in scope, and VV SheetModel exports both (:597-598). ViewportSnapMove also reads viewportCarry (:406), viewportTracking (:368, :516), acquireDwellMs (:375), acquireMax (:347) and trackMarkerSizePx (:254, :317) with no fallback. VV ToolSetup 1.0.0 returns none of them, so the carry would be a silent no-op.
recommendation: WP-S04b-11R: add CarryTarget to VV HitResolution, with GetSelectionItems and IsSelected added to its SheetModel import. Make ToolSetup's five carry reader keys and the AppConfig keys part of the same WP. Accept on 'with ViewportCarry false the plain frame move returns'.

title: Flask drawing-notes route: no Last-Modified, in-place write, no backup

recommendation: GET: serve the notes file's bytes as stored with send_from_directory/send_file (conditional: Last-Modified and ETag come free) plus Cache-Control: no-store, instead of jsonify(json.load(f)); keep 404 {missing:true} for a missing file. Normalise appends non-schema keys in source order (VV Document :175, :184), so a file carrying two or more non-schema keys would compare as moved and the lockstep would raise false questions. title: Flask drawing-notes GET re-serialises with sorted keys
detail: WCP/server.py:803-804 answers GET with jsonify(json.load(f)). The bundled Flask is 3.0.0, whose DefaultJSONProvider.sort_keys is True (flask/json/provider.py:151), and server.py does not override it, so every object comes back with alphabetically sorted keys. Spec Normalise rebuilds the schema keys in a fixed order but appends non-schema keys in source order (VV Document :175, :184), and LockJson compares the result as a string (TV Document :256-268). A group or note carrying two or more non-schema keys would therefore read back differently from what the app wrote, and the lockstep would ask about a file that did not move. Latent today: none of the four VV project notes files carries a non-schema key.
recommendation: In WP-S06b-02 serve GET with send_from_directory (bytes as stored, conditional: Last-Modified and ETag free) instead of jsonify; keep 404 {missing:true}.

title: LF-only tokeniser + autocrlf checkouts: CRLF statements lose every heading, rule and table
detail: Md__Tokenise__ splits lines on LF only (:264) and its block regexes are end-anchored (:65-73). A JS dot does not match a carriage return, so a CRLF statement tokenises as paragraphs and HTML only. RB05's statement is CRLF on disk (2,212 CRLF; git i/lf w/crlf; core.autocrlf=true; text=auto), so TV today renders it with no headings, dividers or tables, and 5 of 7 statement suites fail. VV's repo has the same autocrlf and text=auto settings.
recommendation: Fix in TV first (D-S07b-02), then port. In both repos, add a .gitattributes eol=lf rule for md/html/json under 10__StatementDocs. Make the tokeniser accept CRLF while keeping the source lines byte-exact, and add a CRLF case to RoundTrip. Never normalise on read.
evidence: TV run 01-Oct: RoundTrip 'every heading found (0 of 138)', blocks 'html 107, paragraph 449'. git ls-files --eol RB05_T01_S01: i/lf w/crlf attr/text=auto. VV repo: core.autocrlf=true, '* text=auto'.

title: Keyboard: VV's 3D hotkeys would eat statement typing, and Backspace navigates back
detail:
VV's global hotkey handler (03__AppUtils/Na__AppUtils__ValeVision__HotkeyHandler__.js 1.0.0) treats only input, textarea and select as typing (:53-56, :92). It calls preventDefault() on a match before dispatching (:96), and matches bare keys case-insensitively, without Shift. The dictionary (02__AppData/Na__ValeVision__HotkeysDictionary__.json) gives:
- Swallowed bare keys: r, b, t, y, v, 1-9, PageUp and PageDown.
- Also swallowed: d, o, Delete and Escape. These are documentation entries whose action ValeVision__DrawingMarkup__Contextual has no callback in index.html :1792-1809, so the key is still swallowed, with a console warning.
- F is bound only as Alt+Shift+F (fog), and Backspace only as Alt+Backspace (history.back(), :182-188). Plain Backspace is NOT stolen.
The statement page is contenteditable and does not stop propagation at its root (TV relies on KeyScope + DocumentKeys, v2.110), so typing would lose those letters, digits, Delete and Escape, and Alt+Backspace would leave the app. The Page also imports DocumentKeys statically.
recommendation: Before WP-S07b-05C ships, land KeyScope and the HotkeyHandler gate: one owner among WP-S03a-03 / WP-S05a-01 / WP-S09-05. VV's handler must act only in the model scope and use Na__KeyScope__IsTypingTarget, which counts contenteditable. Also land DocumentKeys 1.1.0 + Na__Hotkeys__DocumentTabs__.json (WP-S03a-09 / WP-S05a-02), and have the ModeController hand over the scope reader. Acceptance: typed r, b, t, y, v, d, o, 1, Delete and Escape stay in the statement, and Alt+Backspace does not navigate.
evidence: VV HotkeyHandler :53-56, :92, :96; dictionary :180-189 (Backspace, AltKey true), :191-200 (F, Alt+Shift), :202-311 (D, O, Arrows, Alt, Shift, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+C/V, Delete, Escape 'Contextual'); VV index.html :1792-1809 callback map (no Contextual callback); TV Statement Page has no root stopPropagation (keys via DocumentKeys, Page :29-36, :167); TV devlog v2.110 :5496-5573.

title: Document Sharing and Statement Data depend on each other; keep Share__Open off VV start-up
detail: The Page imports Share__Button__ (Share in Read). Share__Open__ (:78), Share__Manifest__ (:97-98) and Share__Button__ (:71) import Statement Data back (EnsureLoaded, List, CHANGED_EVENT), and the manifest re-records share links when a statement is published (:450-462). TV starts Share__Open__ from Index.html at start-up (:904). Doing the same in VV would pull Statement Data and its transport onto the start-up path, which defeats the lazy loader.
recommendation: Port Statement Data before or with DocumentSharing (WP-S08-11). Never start Share__Open__ from VV's index.html. Because the editor is lazy, a shared link must itself trigger the load: add a boot-time check of the share parameter that imports nothing from the editor and calls the loader facade (OpenStatements / OpenSpecification / OpenRegister) when a link is present. Share__Open__ then runs inside the loaded editor (S07b-V07, coordinate with WP-S08-11 / WP-S09-12). If statements are ruled out of scope, DocumentSharing needs a statement-free VV adaptation (D-S07b-01).
evidence: Line refs above; VV Loader header: editor modules are only ever import()ed.
verifier_note: 'Start it through the loader once the editor has loaded' is circular for a shared link, because the link is what should load the editor (TV Share__Open__ :67-69, :276, :317-333).

If both approaches are built, VV gets two statement transports.

title: Statement worker routes: store without caching and do not bump the shared build manifest per file
detail: VV's CloudflareHandler__DrawingNotes__ stores with httpMetadata.cacheControl 'no-cache, max-age=0' and calls na_write_build_manifest on every POST (:120-140). That rewrites VaApps/Index/Na__BuildVersion__Manifest__.json with a new unix-time buildVersion (ProjectEditor handler :160-171). VV's ProjectLoader appends that buildVersion as ?v= to every project.json and GLB URL (Na__AppUtils__WithBuildToken :249-252, used at :407-408, :514, :519), so each bump makes every client re-download every project's models on its next load. A statement Publish writes dozens of pictures plus md, html and index; a handler copied from DrawingNotes would bump the global token dozens of times per Publish. Statement reads do not use the token.
recommendation: In CloudflareHandler__StatementDocs__ (or the shim's worker routes): store the index, md and html with cacheControl 'no-cache, max-age=0', the DrawingNotes convention, so a re-publish shows at once. Store pictures with an explicit policy. Do not call na_write_build_manifest per write; at most once, on the index write that Publish makes last, or not at all. Add both rules to WP-S07b-03's acceptance.
evidence: WCP/CloudflareWorker/src/handlers/CloudflareHandler__DrawingNotes__.js :120-140; CloudflareHandler__ProjectEditor__.js :160-171; VV ProjectLoader :56-66, :249-252, :407-408, :514-519.

title: WP-05, WP-06 and WP-07 cannot land separately; the writing surface needs ProjectQrCode
detail:
Internal import graph (01-Oct):
- Page__ imports Publish__ (07), Standard__Registry__ and Standard__DrawingSchedule__Live__ (09).
- Editor__ and Editor__Cards__ import Standard__Registry__.
- The Registry imports all six section modules, including TrueVisionHub__, which statically imports ProjectQr Symbol, Painter and ProjectLink.
- Publish__ imports the Registry and ProjectQr Symbol.
So the original WP-S07b-05 (Page, Editor, Cards...) can neither link nor pass its acceptance before WP-06 and WP-07, and none of them can load before the ProjectQrCode port (WP-S07a-04). By contrast, 18 files have no external imports and can land early as inert modules: Data__Index, Images, the five Md modules, Editor__Move, Editor__Typing, Publish__Page, Contents, DrawingSchedule, Finishes, Header, Footer, the Config JSON and both CSS files.
recommendation:
Re-cut the packages:
- WP-S07b-05A: the pure modules, landed inert.
- WP-S07b-05B: Data, Transport, Reader and Manager, after the transport and config.
- WP-S07b-05C: Registry, Hub, Editor, Cards, Figure, Pdf, Publish, Publish__Images and Page, in one landing after QR, sharing, keys and the menu renderer.
Run Na__Verify__ModuleGraph__.mjs after each.
evidence: Page__.js imports :126-167 (Publish :148, Registry :156, Live :157); Registry :140-143; Editor and Cards import the Registry; Publish :96-97; verify_s07b/internal_graph.py output.

title: Context-menu renderer leaf and its stylesheet have no owning WP
detail: The Statement Page (:159) and Editor__Figure__ import Na__ContextMenu__Ui__Open and Na__ContextMenu__Ui__Close from 27__System__ContextMenuSystem/Na__ContextMenuSystem__Ui__MenuRenderer__.js. Do not port SystemLogic, RightClickGuard, HitResolver or the Sections; the 3D right-click menu is a separate decision (S09/S10).

title: A shared statement link must itself load VV's lazy editor
detail: TV starts Share__Open__ at boot (Index.html :904 import, :1738 call). Share__Open__ imports the ModeController directly (:67-69), reads the open parameter through Share__Links, waits for Na__LeMode__Ready and calls Na__LeMode__OpenStatements({statementId, view:'read'}) (:276, :283, :317-333). S07b-F35 says VV must start Share__Open__ 'through the loader once the editor has loaded', which is circular: in VV nothing loads the editor until a tab is pressed, so a reader opening a shared statement link would land on the 3D view.
recommendation: VV needs a boot-time check of the share parameter that does not import the editor graph (a small leaf, or the loader facade). When a link is present, it calls the loader (Na__LeLoad__OpenStatements / OpenSpecification / OpenRegister, or one generic facade entry) to load the editor; Share__Open__ then runs inside the loaded editor. Own it in WP-S08-11 / WP-S09-12 (index wiring for 66 'via the loader facade'); S07b only supplies the statement entry point.
evidence: TV Index.html :904, :1734-1738; Share__Open__.js :67-89, :270-290, :317-341; VV Loader header (editor modules are only ever import()ed).

detail:

title: VV node suites need the QR port, VV's ProjectLoader seam and a VV address bar

title: Off-localhost acceptance needs a port other than 8000/8090
detail: WP-S07b-06's acceptance reads the Read view 'off localhost (*.localhost host)'. VV's Na__AppUtils__IsRunningOnLocalhost (ProjectLoader :303-307) returns true for port 8000 whatever the hostname (TV's for 8000 and 8090), and WCP Flask binds 127.0.0.1:8000 (server.py :74-75). A *.localhost host served by WCP Flask therefore still counts as localhost. TV proved its reader from 'reader.localhost:8864' (devlog v2.171 :106-110).

title: VV web viewer renders drawings and builds PDFs on the reader's device; TV's published-document system is absent
detail: TV v2.155 split the authoring renderer from a reader that computes nothing (52 reader, 53 schema, 65 publisher) to stop iPhone, iPad and Pixel crashes. VV's viewer (v2.58.0, ported from TV v2.65) still calls SetSheet on Enter and on loaded/active sheet changes. Every viewport is therefore rendered on the reader's device, through VV's composer (DIV-1). The dock PDF button runs the whole exporter on the phone. None of 52, 53 or 65 exists in VV.
recommendation: Port the published system as one programme (WP-S08-05..10): schema, reader, VV transport, publisher, then switch the viewer to published drawings. This is the highest-value alignment in the slice: a parity gap and a reliability fix at once.
evidence: VVM/LE/05__Core__ModeController/Na__LayoutEditor__ModeController__.js:539,779,785; VVM/LE/80__Feature__WebViewer/Na__LayoutEditor__WebViewer__.js:83,289-296; TV ModeController:747-754,1124-1137; TV DEVLOG v2.155 lines 1266-1363
vv_adaptation: Transport, URL resolution, DocumentId, identity strings and loader seams as itemised in the other findings

title: Whitecardopedia project sync would delete every published picture (and likely thumbnails/snapshots) from R2
detail: na_purge_stale_r2_images (WCP/Tools__DevUtils/AutomationUtil__SyncSingleProject__ToCloudAndWeb__Main__.py:659-680) calls list_objects_v2(Bucket, Prefix=f'{r2_prefix}/') with no Delimiter and no continuation token, so it is recursive and sees only the first 1,000 keys. It builds its keep-set from wcp_dir.iterdir() (top-level local images only, :645-656) and deletes every .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp key whose bare file name is not in that set. It runs on every full and images-only sync (:926, :959). The GLB purge (:628-642) lists the prefix the same unscoped way. Published tier pictures, print PNGs and fog masks would vanish on the next sync, leaving manifests that name missing files. The exposure is live today. The local mirror holds 25 PresentationMode/Thumbnails/*.webp across 7 projects and 18 LayoutEditor/Snapshots/*.webp in 2026/3047__Doous, and each is a deletion candidate on R2 at the next sync of its project. Those files are committed to git, so once pushed the app would fall back to GitHub Pages: degraded, not blank. Published files and S07a's planned sheet images would have no such fallback. Read, not run. The bucket was not listed, so whether anything has already been deleted is unknown.
recommendation: Fix this now, independent of publishing: WP-S08-04 should run first in the whole programme. List top-level keys only (Delimiter='/') with pagination, in both the image purge and the GLB purge. Optionally also skip the 06__Layout__PublishedDocuments/, LayoutEditor/, PresentationMode/ and 00__* prefixes. This is a shared Vale pipeline, so Adam approves it (D-S08-09). The fix blocks VV's first R2 publish and S07a's sheet-image R2 writes.
evidence: WCP/Tools__DevUtils/AutomationUtil__SyncSingleProject__ToCloudAndWeb__Main__.py:645-656 (keep-set from iterdir), :659-680 (purge; list_objects_v2 Prefix only at :667), called :926 and :959; R2_BASE_PREFIX :101
vv_adaptation: VV-only pipeline; TV avoids this by skipping 00__ folders and never sweeping published roots
verifier_note: Re-read the code. The exposure exists today for existing VV assets, not only after publishing. This raises the urgency of WP-S08-04. | The bug already affects mirrored thumbnails and snapshots, and it would also delete S07a's sheet images.

title: 53__Data__Layout__PublishedSchema (the shared publish/read contract) is absent
detail: 4 files: JSON (189 lines), Paths 1.1.0 (678), Version 1.0.0 (172) and README (99). They hold every folder and file name, the element kinds, the tier table (Fit 2, Read 6, Detail 12, Print 20 px/mm), the version gate (schema 1; refuses newer and older with a human reason), the Stamp and ShareLinksPath (v2.166, additive). The readable schema is TV's AA00 example folder in the project portal. Top-level number 53 is free in VV.

title: 52__System__Layout__PublishedDocuments (the reader) is absent
detail: 11 files, 3,998 lines: Document (loads the index, then the manifest, sheet and element files, and builds one SVG string with progress events), Urls (R2 first on the live site, repository first on localhost, a 404 never retried), Viewports (tier ladder, 128 MB decoded budget, no decode retry), Sheet/Paint/Elements/Unpublished (mark emitter, grey mask), LoadingScreen (v2.156), Config, CSS and README. It imports only 53 and ProjectLoader, and its test proves no renderer is reachable.
recommendation: Port at top level 52. Verbatim except Na__PubDoc__Urls__ (VV project resolution; on localhost the Flask copy first) and Na__PubDoc__Config__.json (Sheet__FontFamily = the VV authoring face; prefixes). Leave Na__PubDoc__Styles__Main__.css unlinked, as TV does.
evidence: TVM/52__.../README__PublishedDocuments__.md; Na__PubDoc__Urls__.js:142-207; Na__PubDoc__Config__.json PubDoc__Sheet__Config.Sheet__FontFamily (must match the authoring side)
vv_adaptation:
- Urls.FromPage: use the VV ProjectLoader facades.
- Urls.For on localhost: ${origin}/Projects/{folderId}/{path} (the Flask copy) first, then R2, then GitHub Pages.
- Urls.For on the live site: R2 first, then GitHub Pages. Build the R2 URL from the configured R2 base (AppConfig ProjectData__AssetUrls__R2BaseUrl). Never route it through Na__AppUtils__ResolveAssetUrl: its hasImages_R2:false gate sends 11 projects to GitHub Pages only (S08-V02).
- Config Sheet__FontFamily: verbatim ('Open Sans', ...) only if D-S08-03 (a) lands before the first publish. Otherwise use VV's Helvetica stack, because element text is line-broken at publish with the authoring metrics.
- Meta__SchemaRef and Debug__PrefixNote.
- [TrueVision3D PubDoc] console prefixes in Document, Elements, Sheet and Urls.
- README paths.
verifier_note: The hasImages_R2 trap was missed. The font setting depends on the order in which WP-S08-03 and the first publish land.

title: Publisher orchestration (Publish__ 1.1.0 + Publish__Config) is absent
detail: Publish__.js (707 lines) does the whole publish: per-sheet status; a new revision archived to a zip (never overwritten); sheet and element files; per-viewport bake; the baked PDF (strict:false, FAST); the manifest last; a document-scoped prune. With R2 ticked it uploads, lists back and checks sizes, uploads the manifest, then prunes. Orphans are retired only on a full publish. The unpublished file and share record go just before the index, and the index goes last. Config: PushToR2Default false, BakePdf, RetireOrphans, SpecLoadTimeoutMs, labels.

evidence: TVM/LE/65__.../Na__LayoutEditor__Publish__.js:249-431 (PublishOne), 572-681 (PublishSheets), 635-670 (index last), 99 (appVersion floor), 257 (register wording)

- appVersion floor (:99) and Behaviour__AppVersion: the VV release.
- Console prefixes.
- Meta__SchemaRef, written into every manifest (:355), the index (:522) and the unpublished file (:549): point it at the VV example folder.

- Project__ContentFolder (:527): '06__Layout__PublishedDocuments'.

title: Bakers Publish__Raster, Publish__Sheet and Publish__Viewports are absent and import TV-only exports
detail: Raster 1.0.0 cuts one render into four tiers by halvings, makes the fog mask and SHA-256 names, and refuses a browser that writes PNG for WebP. Sheet 1.0.0 writes element files with resolved keys and per-layer editor SVG, plus portable images. Viewports 1.1.0 writes the picture, linework SVG, fog masks and holed site faces (v2.160). Sheet and Viewports import PaintOrder, BuildLayerPrimitives, BuildViewportFrame, ShapeRings, FloorAreas, RenderFogForExport, SitePlanDrawing and IsSitePlanViewport. VV has none of these, so a verbatim copy fails to link.

- Viewports: verbatim below the header once the owning slices deliver BuildViewportFrame, FacesFromRings, RenderFogForExport, SitePlanDrawing and IsSitePlanViewport. Alternatively use D-S08-11 stubs, for fog and site plans only.
- Sheet: port_adapted. Replace Meta__SchemaRef (:271, :408) and the 'Published by TrueVision' Meta__Note (:272). Set Na__LePubSheet__IMAGES_DIR (:81) to VV's sheet-image folder per D-S08-14, agreed with S07a. Sheet also needs PaintOrder, BuildLayerPrimitives and FloorAreas.

It also hard-codes IMAGES_DIR='05__Layout__DrawingDocs__Images' (:81), which conflicts with S07a's D-S07a-07. | Separates the parts that really are verbatim from the identity strings and the images folder seam. | 'Header only once dependencies exist' was wrong for Publish__Sheet.

title: Publish__Transport must be re-pointed at VV's Flask blueprint and VV's worker
detail: TV Transport 1.0.0 posts to /api/truevision/published/* on the 8090 server and reaches R2 through Na__CfApi__UploadPublished, ListPublished and DeletePublished (the generic /r2/*). VV has neither. TV's R2Ready() is synchronous and is called without await (Publish__.js:585 and the share manifest), whereas VV's worker config arrives asynchronously from Flask GET /api/editor-config.
recommendation: Port with identical exports: API constant /api/valevision/published, R2 calls through the new VV client util. Prefetch the worker config in LocalReady so R2Ready answers synchronously from the cache. The restart hint names WCP/server.py.
evidence: TVM/LE/65__.../Publish__Transport__.js:43-46,55,98-108,202-206; TV Publish__.js:585; VVM/03__AppUtils/Na__AppUtils__R2SaveProjectJson__.js:96,233
vv_adaptation: Local API base and R2 client swapped; sync R2Ready from a cached config

title: VV worker needs published-document routes (file, list, scoped delete) in VV's own storage
detail: whitecardopedia-editor-api has only semantic routes. Its asset route takes JSON base64 (25 MB cap), is guarded to Thumbnails/Linework/Snapshots, sets no-cache and bumps the global build manifest. Publishing needs raw files up to tens of MB, a list with sizes, a scoped delete and per-class Cache-Control. Key: VaApps/Projects/{folderId}/06__Layout__PublishedDocuments/<rel>. Routes: POST .../published/file?path= (raw, about 95 MB), POST .../published/list {document,cursor} and POST .../published/delete {document,paths}.
recommendation: New handler CloudflareHandler__PublishedDocuments__.js, with routes in index.js before the greedy save route, using the existing X-Editor-Api-Key and CORS helper (POST avoids a CORS change). Enforce the document scope server-side. Adam deploys with wrangler.
evidence: WCP/CloudflareWorker/src/index.js:112-116,148,160-214; handlers/CloudflareHandler__ProjectAsset__.js:51-52,140-148; CloudflareHelper__Cors__.js:72 (GET, POST, OPTIONS)
vv_adaptation:
- Semantic, authenticated routes instead of TV's open generic /r2/*.
- Content type taken from the extension.
- Cache-Control: immutable for __<10 hex> names, otherwise max-age=60 must-revalidate. No build-manifest bump.
- folderId guard: either admit the three legacy folder names that contain a space (2025/FN-62104__Fenner Scheme-01/-02/-03), or refuse them with a stated reason (S08-V06).
- W2/W3 document guard: TV's DOCUMENT_PATTERN ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_\-]{2,79}$, which is stricter than the segment regex.
- At most six path segments.
- Both workers bind the same bucket, noble-architecture-cdn, so keep VV's routes on VV's worker only.
verifier_note: The proposed guards would refuse three real VV projects. The document guard must match the Flask archive/prune pattern. The shared bucket was not noted.

title: VV Flask mirror for local filing (list, read, write, archive, prune)
detail: TV's local filing is ProjectVision__TrueVisionPublished__Api__.py (448 lines): segment, project and extension guards, byte sniffing, atomic temp-then-rename writes, archive zips that are never overwritten, document-scoped prune, 2-digit year, 256 MB cap. VV's Flask registers only the scrapbook blueprint. server.py get_project_path joins ids containing '/' with no inside-the-tree check.
recommendation: New WCP/Server__ValeVisionPublished__Api__.py, a port of TV's: /api/valevision/published/{list,file,archive,prune} with the same query shape, YEAR ^\d{4}$, root Projects/{year}/{folder}/06__Layout__PublishedDocuments and its own guarded resolver. Register it in server.py and restart.
evidence: NAAPPS/ProjectVision__TrueVisionPublished__Api__.py:39-45 routes, 86-93 patterns, 350-446 archive/prune; WCP/server.py:91-97 (blueprint), 128-160 (get_project_path)
vv_adaptation:
- Route prefix: /api/valevision/published.
- YEAR_PATTERN: ^\d{4}$.
- Root: WCP/Projects/{year}/{folder}/06__Layout__PublishedDocuments, behind its own guarded resolver (not get_project_path).
- PROJECT_PATTERN: must admit, or explicitly refuse, the three 2025 Fenner folders whose names contain a space.
- Keep unchanged: DOCUMENT_PATTERN, SEGMENT_PATTERN, the six-segment limit, the extension allowlist, byte sniffing, atomic writes, the never-overwrite archive and the document-scoped prune.
verifier_note: The folder-name and document-id patterns were not called out.

title: A published write must never bump VV's global build manifest
detail: The ProjectAsset and DrawingNotes handlers call na_write_build_manifest, which rewrites the global VaApps/Index/Na__BuildVersion__Manifest__.json. ProjectLoader appends ?v=<buildVersion> to every project.json and GLB URL. Each bump therefore makes every Vale client re-download its models, across all projects. Published files are content-hashed or short-lived JSON and need no bump.
recommendation: The published handler must not call na_write_build_manifest. Set Cache-Control per file class instead: immutable for hashed names, 60 s must-revalidate for the index, manifests and element files.
evidence: WCP/CloudflareWorker/src/handlers/CloudflareHandler__ProjectEditor__.js:59,160-171; CloudflareHandler__ProjectAsset__.js:148; VVM/03__AppUtils/Na__AppUtils__ProjectLoader.js:251-254,407-408,497-519
vv_adaptation: TV policy: ApiClient 1001-1007 (immutable vs max-age=60)

title: VV has no document id, yet it names every published folder, archive and share fallback
detail: TV's Na__LeModel__GetDocumentId returns the stored Sheet__Fields__DocumentId, else project code + phase + number (SheetRecords 1604-1608). Published folders, archive zips, manifests, index rows, the WebViewer and the Share fallback all use it. VV has only the Drawing No. (stored, else '<code>-<order>'), no phase and no register. The PDF exporter already diverges here (VV fields.DrawingNumber vs TV fields.DocumentId).
recommendation:
Decide this before the first publish, and decide it once together with D-S03b-01 and S07a's register port (WP-S07a-01 switches the title block to DocumentId).
- If the register/phase port is scheduled before the publisher: port TV's Na__LeModel__GetDocumentId directly and skip any interim adapter.
- Otherwise: an interim VV Na__LeModel__GetDocumentId returns the stored Drawing No., falling back to the existing '<code>-<order>' default. Sanitise it to TV's local DOCUMENT_PATTERN ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_\-]{2,79}$ (no dot, 3-80 characters). The archive and prune routes refuse anything else, while the publisher only checks the looser segment regex (53/Paths__.js:107, 250-251).

Changing the id later creates new published folders and archives the old ones.
evidence: TVM/LE/07__Core__SheetData/Na__LayoutEditor__SheetRecords__.js:1604-1608; VVM/LE/07__.../SheetRecords__.js:730-738; VVM/LE/60__.../PdfExporter__.js:248 vs TV :477
vv_adaptation: Adapter returning the drawing number; must pass the schema segment regex
verifier_note: The same decision appears in S03b and S07a. The stricter local pattern would otherwise fail a publish half-way.

title: PdfExporter TV 1.12.0 vs VV 1.2.0
detail:
VV lacks these TV changes:
- 1.0.3: design phase (v2.32).
- 1.2.0 and 1.12.0: site plans (v2.49, v2.160).
- 1.4.0: Open Sans.
- 1.6.0: fog (v2.94).
- 1.7.0: Layers-list paint order with per-viewport frames (v2.106).
- 1.8.0: sheet pictures (v2.116).
- 1.9.0: turned viewports (v2.138).
- 1.10.0: overspill regions (v2.143).
- 1.11.0: FAST packing and options (v2.155).
- The LoadLibrary export and the returnPromise save.

The two apps number their versions separately. VV's header logs VV 1.0.3 (composite weights), VV 1.1.0 (style bands, from TV Edge Styles) and VV 1.2.0 (ExportRectMm, 'Ported from TrueVision3D (PdfExporter 1.3.0, v2.50.0)'). So VV does log TV 1.3.0's change. VV also has the behaviour of TV 1.1.0 (spec wait) and TV 1.5.0 (named file) without header entries. 'VV 1.2.0' therefore does not mean VV has TV 1.0.x-1.2.0.
recommendation: Two steps. Now: the independent 1.11.0 parts (WP-S08-02). Later: port_whole_reapply_vv once PaintOrder, MarkupBridge 1.20, SheetChrome 1.14, ShapeRings, Hatch, SheetImages, ViewportRotation, fog, site plans and ModelSource land (WP-S08-14).
evidence: drift_all: 585 vs 339 lines, 364 diff; TV PdfExporter__.js:44-130 DEVELOPMENT LOG, :386-399 AddPicture, :495-541 BuildDocument; VV :38-58, :266-297
vv_adaptation: Console prefix; subject 'ValeVision3D sheet'; 42__System__DrawingViewCore path; filename code = fields.DrawingNumber until D-S08-06
verifier_note: The survey said VV's header does not log TV 1.3.0, but it does (as VV 1.2.0). The version numbers collide between apps and could mislead a swarm agent.

title: PdfFonts absent: VV prints non-embedded Helvetica (deliberate divergence to revisit)
detail:
Ledger row 1169 calls the Helvetica PDF face deliberate, but everything else in VV points to Open Sans:
- VV D14 says Open Sans 300/400/600.

title: VV share links: a bare project code is ambiguous, and TV's link builder rejects VV's usual ?project= value
detail:

The code collides. 13 VV numeric project codes are shared by two or three projects (schemes) in the master index: 3038 (Gordon Scheme-03/-04), 55164, 56662, 57994, 59908, 61511, 61721, 61922, 62104 (three Fenner schemes), 62361, 63568, 63578 (Yates Orangery/Porch) and 63592. LookupIndexEntry resolves a bare code to one of them: the newest year wins, and on a tie the later index entry wins. Sheet ids repeat across projects, so ?project=3038&open=Sheet_004 can silently open the other scheme's drawing.

VV's ?project= is normally the folderId. Whitecardopedia opens VV with ?project=<folderId>, and VV's own R2 rule requires that form. TV's Na__LeShareLink__CurrentProject keeps the raw GetProjectCodeFromUrl() only if it matches CODE_PATTERN ^[A-Za-z0-9]{2,12}$. '2026/3047__Doous' fails, so UrlFor returns '' and every Share button hands out no link in a session opened from Whitecardopedia.
recommendation:
Decide D-S08-13. Carry the folderId (canonical and unique) or the folder name without the year as the project token: <VV live app URL>?project={folderId}&open={documentKey}. Adapt Share__Links:
- CurrentProject: take the resolved folderId; use the index entry's projectCode for display only.
- Replace CODE_PATTERN with a project-token pattern that admits '/', '_', '-', '.' and the three space-containing legacy folders.
- Replace the NA built-in floor.

Keep the document keys and the open parameter verbatim. Trade-off for Adam: a folderId link breaks if the project is later renamed; a code link survives renames but is ambiguous for 13 codes.

detail: TV keeps 8 dev-owned top-level keys in three lists: Na__DevSavedKeys (localhost overlay, LoadingSequence:352-361), DEV_OWNED_PROJECT_DATA_KEYS (ModelSync:121-130) and TRUEVISION_DEV_OWNED_KEYS (BuildScript:83-92). title: Shared Whitecardopedia registrar lacks TV registrar 1.1.0-1.3.0: reloads over unsaved work and on a first install
detail: VV runs under Whitecardopedia's registrar (VV index.html 44). Its controllerchange bridge (registrar 110-150) reloads the page once per session whenever a worker takes control, deferring only for Na__LoadWatchdog__IsLoadingActive. TV's registrar 1.1.0 (19-Sep) also waits while the Layout Editor has unsaved work (window.TrueVision__Pwa__HasUnsavedWork, published by AutoSave); 1.2.0 (19-Sep, TV v2.75.0) does not reload on a FIRST install, so a first visit (and the first launch of an installed iPad icon) does not load the model twice; 1.3.0 (29-Sep) registers with updateViaCache 'none' so a token bump is seen at once. The WCP registrar has none of the three (it registers with { scope } only, line 195; its log stops at 1.2.0 of 26-Jun). VV deliberately did not publish an unsaved flag on the belief that it has no worker (ledger row 236; VV AutoSave 48-53). Consequences: every first VV visit loads the model, reloads and loads it again; and any token bump (S10-F17) reloads open VV pages over unsaved sheets, under the close guard's leave-site question.
recommendation: Port the three TV registrar changes into the WCP registrar (Vale's own infrastructure; WP-S10-15) and publish a neutral window.Na__Pwa__HasUnsavedWork from VV AutoSave (Na__LeAuto__HasUnsavedWork is already exported; the name per S03b D-S03b-07). Land before any token bump under D-S10-13. Test Whitecardopedia's own pages as well, since the registrar is shared.
evidence: WCP Whitecardopedia__Pwa__ServiceWorker__Registrar__.js 28-46 (log), 110-150 (bridge), 195 (register); TV TrueVision__Pwa__ServiceWorker__Registrar__.js 36-62 (log 1.1.0-1.3.0), 125-200; TV AutoSave PublishUnsavedFlag ~560-570; VV AutoSave 48-53, 345, 433; ledger 135-173 and row 236; TV devlog v2.75.0 lines 9189, 9201

VV's scrapbook port already had to parse every answer defensively.

It cannot change the /api/projects/ captures, which win as more specific rules. So the VV facade and ported modules must also treat 'JSON 404 Project not found' on a sub-route, HTML, 405 and non-JSON as 'route missing'. Keep the parsing defensive.

title: Port SheetRecords before features that add record keys or enum values
detail: VV's sheet normaliser fills and resets values it does not know (title block style, paper size, default layers) and is far behind TV (1.15.0 vs 1.39.0). If a feature that writes new record keys or enum values lands before the normaliser, VV's next load-and-save silently resets or drops them - persistence loss inside VV's own data.
recommendation: Sequence: port SheetRecords (S03b) with or before any feature that adds record fields or enum values; add a normalise-save-reload round-trip check per added field.

title: CrossSection__SceneData per-scene entries differ between the apps; TD06 is not met
detail: The two apps share only the block keys (__Description, __Version, __Scenes). VV's 41 SceneData stores each scene as CrossSection__SceneBinding__{SceneId, UpdatedIso, GizmosVisible, SliceDepthM, FillColor, LineColor, LineWidthPx, Sections[CrossSection__Section__{Name, Mode, NormalXyz, PositionMm, Enabled, GizmoVisible}]} and reads back only that form; all 5 VV project.json files carrying the block use it. TV's 41 SceneData stores the raw Serialize() snapshot {gizmosVisible, sliceDepthM, fillColor, lineColor, lineWidthPx, sections[{name, mode, normalXyz, positionMm, enabled, gizmoVisible}], sceneId}, and Apply reads only that. TV plan s3.2 documented VV's IN-MEMORY snapshot (VV SystemLogic Na__CrossSection__SerializeSections, camelCase) as VV's stored schema. Each app reads the other's entries as an empty sections array, i.e. 'no cuts'. No TV repository file carries the block (0/8), so no shared data is broken today. The S12 report (b.1 item 10, F32, F46, module table) repeated 'byte-compatible'.
recommendation: VV: keep its own 41 SceneData writer and reader (DIV-2), and never port TV 41 Na__SectionCut__SceneData__ or Serialize__ into VV. ProjectData only passes the block through, so F46's registration is unaffected. TV back-port (D-S12-V02): CaptureForScene maps the snapshot to VV's prefixed entry keys, and RestoreForScene reads the prefixed form, falling back to camelCase; correct TV plan s3.2.

title: project.json folderId is unreliable: never use it for R2 or disk paths
detail: Census of the 155 local WCP/Projects/*/*/project.json files (01-Oct-2026): folderId equals the real year/folder in 91, is missing in 10 (e.g. 2026/44371__Gill) and differs in 54 (e.g. 2025/43822__Napthine stores '43822__Napthine' with no year; 2025/59494__Weeks stores '2025/WK-3007__Weeks', an old name). Report b.4 told the facade to 'prefer GetLoadedProjectData().folderId when set', which would send a third of projects' writes to R2 prefixes the app never reads. Every existing VV client (R2SaveProjectJson, R2AssetUpload, R2DrawingNotes) resolves through Na__AppUtils__NormalizeProjectFolderId(?project) and the master index. Whitecardopedia opens VV with ?project=<folderId> taken from the folder it loaded (WCP 03__AppData/Na__AppData__ProjectLoader.js:519 overwrites the file's value), so the URL token is reliable. NormalizeProjectFolderId still guesses '2026/<code>' when the index has no entry (ProjectLoader.js:350). Corroborates S07a-V05.
recommendation: The facade and the ProjectLoader helpers resolve the folder only from the URL token via the master index (LookupIndexEntry), refuse writes when it misses (no '2026/<code>' guess), and never read project.json's folderId. Add a facade test with a stale-folderId fixture. Cleaning the field in the data is Adam's call.
evidence: parity/verify_s12_r2/folderid_field.py (91 same / 10 missing / 54 differ); VV 03/Na__AppUtils__ProjectLoader.js:335-351; WCP 61__Feature__PwaAppHelpers/Na__Feature__PwaAppHelpers__ValeVisionLinkRouting__Logic__.js:37-54; WCP 03__AppData/Na__AppData__ProjectLoader.js:508-519; report b.4 pre-verification text

title: Printed project name never fills: VV reads a TV-only global, and both apps read the presentation block
detail: VV's already-ported SpecPdf__.js:147-148 reads window.TrueVision__Pwa__ProjectContext; so do TV's SpecDocument__.js:161, Register__Pdf__.js:213 and Panel__ScrapbookParametric__.js:290. Only TV's 62__Feature__AppInstallability/TrueVision__Pwa__ProjectContext__.js defines it, and nothing in VV or Whitecardopedia does, so VV's specification PDF never prints a project name today. Separately, the title block's Project default (Na__LeRec__BuildFields: VV SheetRecords__.js:768-769, TV :1683-1684, identical) reads projectName || displayName from Na__PresentationMode__ProjectJson__GetActiveConfig(). That is the PresentationMode__SavedCameraScenes block, and 0/9 VV and 0/3 TV presentation blocks carry a name, so the default never fills in either app. This is the same root cause as F24. S07a-V05 recommended GetActiveConfig().projectName as VV's name source; it is always empty.
recommendation: WP-S12-V18: one VV project-facts seam (the facade's Na__CfApi__ProjectDisplayName(): root projectName 155/155, displayName 31/155, projectNameAlias 7/155, with an agreed precedence), used by SpecPdf, SpecDocument, Register Pdf, ScrapbookParametric and BuildFields. Offer the BuildFields fix and the helper back to TV.

detail: Facade/shims: WP-S12-05, WP-S09-06, WP-S07a-02 (register facade), WP-S08-06 (R2PublishedDocs client and ProjectLoader helpers). Flask core: WP-S12-03, WP-S09-06, WP-S03b-05, WP-S06b-02. Blueprints: WP-S12-11/12/13/14 against WP-S07a-06, WP-S08-05, WP-S07b-03, WP-S06b-09. Persistence core: WP-S12-07/08 against WP-S03b-05. Service worker: WP-S12-15, WP-S08-12, WP-S09-11.
